facts.statement: Brasileodactylus is a pterosaur found in the lower Santana Formation of the Aptian stage in the Chapada do Araripe, Ceará, Brazil.
facts.quote: Brasileodactylus (significa en gr. "dedo de Brasil") es el nombre asignado a los restos de un pterosaurio (reptil volador) de la zona inferior de la formación Santana del Aptiense (Cretácico Inferior) de Chapada do Araripe, Ceará, en Brasil.

facts.statement: The genus Brasileodactylus was named by paleontologist Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner in 1984.
facts.quote: El género fue nombrado por el paleontólogo Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner en 1984.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, MN 4804-V, consists of the front part of a jaw.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MN 4804-V, es la parte frontal de la mandíbula.

facts.statement: Brasileodactylus was a medium-sized pterosaur with a wingspan of approximately four meters.
facts.quote: Brasileodactylus era un pterosaurio mediano con una envergadura de aproximadamente cuatro metros.

facts.statement: It had a long, pointed snout and conical teeth that were long and thin at the front ends of the jaws.
facts.quote: Tenía un largo hocico aguzado y dientes cónicos que eran largos y delgados en el extremo frontal de las mandíbulas.

facts.statement: Unlike other Brazilian pterosaurs, it lacked a crest on the snout or lower jaw, though it may have had one on the back of the skull.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros pterosaurios brasileños no poseía cresta sobre el hocico o la mandíbula inferior pero pudo haber tenido una en la parte posterior del cráneo.

facts.statement: Kellner initially assigned Brasileodactylus to the family Ornithocheiridae.
facts.quote: Kellner asignó inicialmente a Brasileodactylus a la familia Ornithocheiridae.

facts.statement: In 1991, Kellner cautiously reclassified it as a Pterodactyloidea of uncertain placement.
facts.quote: En 1991 él cautelosamente lo cambió a un Pterodactyloidea incertae sedis.

facts.statement: In 2000, Kellner claimed it had a close affinity to the Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: En 2000 Kellner afirmó que tenía una cercana afinidad a los Anhangueridae.

facts.statement: David Unwin considered in 2001 that it belonged to the genus Anhanguera but later retracted this view.
facts.quote: David Unwin en 2001 consideró que formaba parte del género Anhanguera pero más tarde se retractó.

facts.statement: Eberhard Frey considered it a species of Coloborhynchus in 2003.
facts.quote: Eberhard Frey en 2003 lo consideró como una especie de Coloborhynchus.

facts.statement: In 2007, Unwin and David Martill suggested that Ludodactylus was a more modern synonym of Brasileodactylus.
facts.quote: En 2007 Unwin y David Martill sugirieron que Ludodactylus era un sinónimo más moderno de Brasileodactylus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Brasileodactylus is Ornithocheiroidea.
Brasileodactylus is classified in the class Reptilia.
Brasileodactylus lived during the Aptian stage, between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2026 study describes a lower jaw of Brasileodactylus araripensis from the Romualdo Formation that provides evidence of a mandibular crest.
facts.quote: A lower jaw of Brasileodactylus araripensis providing evidence of presence of mandibular crest in the studied pterosaur is described from the Romualdo Formation by Nascimento et al. (2026).

rejected.statement: The genus Brasileodactylus was named by Alexander Wilhelm Armin Kellner in 1984.
Brasileodactylus lived during the Early Cretaceous (Aptian age) in the Chapada do Araripe region of Ceará, Brazil.
rejected.quote: Brasileodactylus is an extinct genus of anhanguerian pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian age) lower Santana Formation of Chapada do Araripe, Ceará, Brazil.

rejected.statement: The name Brasileodactylus translates to 'pterosaur from Brazil' and refers to the wing finger of pterosaurs.
rejected.quote: The genus name means 'pterosaur (literally, [wing] "finger") from Brazil'.

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen of Brasileodactylus consists of the front part of a mandible.
rejected.quote: The holotype, MN 4804-V, is the front part of a mandible.

rejected.statement: A specimen designated Brasileodactylus sp. indet. includes a skull that is 429 mm long along with a mandible and proximal left wing.
rejected.quote: AMNH 24444, a 429 mm long skull, with mandible and proximal left wing.

rejected.statement: A skull and articulated lower jaw measuring 57 cm in length, formerly known as Cearadactylus atrox, was discovered in the Romualdo Formation of the Araripe plateau.
rejected.quote: A pterosaur skull, MN 7019-V (formerly CB-PV-F-O93), was discovered in the Romualdo Formation of the Santana Group in the Araripe plateau of northeastern Brazil. It consists of a single skull and articulated lower jaw with a length of 57 cm.

rejected.statement: The pterosaur Cearadactylus, later synonymized with Brasileodactylus, appeared in the novel Jurassic Park in 1990.
rejected.quote: In 1990, Cearadactylus appeared in the famous novel Jurassic Park.

rejected.statement: A 2025 study concluded that the genus Cearadactylus is not distinct and is a synonym of Brasileodactylus.
rejected.quote: In 2025 a study by Rubi V. Pegas and colleagues was published concluding that Cearadactylus was not a distinct genus but a synonym of Brasileodactylus.

rejected.statement: Brasileodactylus was a medium-sized pterosaur with a wingspan of about 4 meters and a body mass of 10 kilograms.
rejected.quote: Brasileodactylus is a medium-sized pterosaur with a wingspan of approximately 4 m and a body mass of 10 kg.

rejected.statement: Brasileodactylus possessed a long pointed snout and conical teeth that were long, thin, and forward-pointing at the front of the jaws.
rejected.quote: It had a long pointed snout and conical teeth that in the extreme front of the jaws were long, thin and forward pointing.

rejected.statement: A specimen described in 2026 revealed that Brasileodactylus had a low, thin crest on the mandible.
rejected.quote: A new specimen described in 2026 revealed the presence of a low, thin crest on the mandible.

rejected.statement: Kellner initially classified Brasileodactylus in Ornithocheiridae, later moved it to Pterodactyloidea incertae sedis, and eventually affirmed a close relationship to Anhangueridae.
rejected.quote: Kellner first assigned Brasileodactylus to the Ornithocheiridae. In 1991, he changed that to the more cautious Pterodactyloidea incertae sedis. In 2000, he affirmed a close affinity to the Anhangueridae.

rejected.statement: A 2019 analysis placed Cearadactylus in a derived position within Anhangueria, just outside the clade Ornithocheirae.
rejected.quote: A 2019 phylogenetic analysis by Adele H. Pentland and colleagues found Cearadactylus in a derived position within the Anhangueria, just outside the Ornithocheirae, which, by their definition, is the clade that contains the families Ornithocheiridae and Anhangueridae.

rejected.statement: Studies combining Brasileodactylus and Cearadactylus fossils support a sister relationship between them and the genus Maraadactylus.
rejected.quote: Studies based on the combined Brasileodactylus and Cearadactylus hypodigm have also supported a sister relationship with Maraadactylus.

rejected.statement: It is debated whether some more complete specimens assigned to Brasileodactylus actually belong to other pterosaurs like Barbosania.
rejected.quote: The last two specimens have been assigned to a Brasileodactylus sp. indet. by André Jacques Veldmeijer. However, some of the more complete specimens may belong to other pterosaurs, such as Barbosania.

rejected.statement: Researchers suggest that the crest on the mandible of Brasileodactylus may have developed as the animal matured.
rejected.quote: The maturity of this specimen compared to others of this genus may suggest that the crest developed through ontogeny.
